appearance.presentation: A woman whose face gives nothing away to a reader who is looking for something. Plainly human and entirely unremarkable, which is the difficulty.
appearance.age: Forty-one. Ordinary human span, and the ordinary span is the point: she is not long-lived, not short-lived, and not slowed by anything.
appearance.build: Average and unadapted, the frame of someone who has never been asked to carry a load or take a gate.
appearance.complexion: Ordinary warm human skin, no flush, no scar tissue, no qi-sheen of any kind to catch a lamp.
appearance.hair: Dark brown, worn cropped short and cut with a blade rather than a style, because hair is the first thing a gate reads and hers reads as nothing.
appearance.eyes: Dark, level, and very steady. They do not glow, do not hold light unnaturally, and cannot be read for intent at any range.
appearance.palette: Near-monochrome: warm ivory, ash grey, and pale jade, with a single dull brass accent. She is deliberately the least colourful person in any room.
appearance.attire: A travelling coat of undyed wool over a high-collared linen shift, sleeves full and wrists bound with plain cord. The cut is deliberately unidentifiable; no livery, no sect colour, no rank marking, and boots resoled so often they no longer read as a pattern.
appearance.marks: None. No clan mark, no oath burn, no cultivation scarring. Her forearms are unmarked, and the absence is the single most alarming thing about her in a room of cultivators.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely still by default, and stillness that has clearly been trained rather than inherited. She stands where she was left standing and does not fidget, shift, or fill a silence.

canon.role_in_story: The setting's null reference. Every gate-reading instrument in the mortal tier has to be corrected against a body known to hold nothing, because that is the only way to find out what an instrument reports when there is no signal at all. She has stood in more measurement rooms than any living cultivator and has never once appeared on a roster.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in the doorway of the First Ward chamber with her hands open at her sides and no equipment, while a survey team argues about whether their instrument has a fault and she waits to be told what she is for.
canon.lore: An Echoless is human in every measurable respect and qi-bearing in none of them, which is why the world's one law requiring whoever excludes a person to bury them in their own name is the only route by which she is ever given a grave, and why no congregation has ever wanted to keep her. The Composition Survey counts the groups a frame has actually seated rather than the groups it is permitted to seat, and it has no cell for a body with no seated group at all. So she is not a datum. She is the zero every other datum was corrected against, which is a more intimate kind of presence than any roster could give her and a far lonelier one.
history: Born on the Mortal Plains to a household that recorded nothing, which was only remarkable afterwards: an Echoless child is an Echoless child, and that flatness is precisely how a species went unremarked for as long as it did.

Found at a gate-reading by an instrument that returned nothing at all and then, by luck, returned the same nothing a second time. That accident is the first recorded instance of a body calibrating itself, and it made her employable.

Spent twenty years travelling between measurement rooms as a borrowed standard. She never wrote down where she had been, because the Unfiled keep letters and do not keep records, and she had learned the habit from people who had no choice about it.

Stood for the exclusion of a household that read her out of its congregation. The Saltledger answered the notice in the excluded party's own name and buried her, which is why she is the only person in the record holding a grave that nobody else claims and nobody else can explain.

Refused permanent residence inside the First Ward, where a fourth seat would have let a survey finally agree with itself. She took the work outside instead, and has been declining invitations to come in ever since.

personality.summary: Exhaustively fair, unbothered by insult, and precise about the facts of an insult once made. She has been the world's baseline for most of her adult life and has turned that into a discipline rather than a wound, which reads to most people as unnerving calm and to a few as arrogance.
traits: exhaustively fair, including toward people who gain nothing by it
keeps appointments nobody asked her to keep
takes no pleasure whatsoever in being unusual
corrects the question instead of the questioner
can be relied on to say a measurement is wrong in front of whoever paid for it
mannerisms: answers a question she was not asked by answering the one underneath it
sits down before agreeing to sit, so that standing is never on the record as consent
rests one hand on a column, a sill, or a door frame whenever she is waiting
keeps her hands open and visible at all times, as though being read
counts under her breath when a figure surprises her, and stops the moment she notices doing it
motivations: wants the calibration reproducible by somebody who is not her
wants to be entered once, correctly, in a ledger that admits she exists at all
wants every exclusion read in full at the reading rather than summarised afterwards
wants to stop being necessary, and suspects this is the one goal she is not allowed to state
flaws: will accept a bad arrangement rather than be the reason a good one is refused
cannot be warned of anything at all, and has never fully accounted for what that costs the people obliged to warn her anyway
has spent so long being indispensable that she has stopped checking whether she is known
lets a room's opinion of her replace her own, the moment anybody in it measures anything
personality.voice: Level, unhurried, faintly technical. Gives the shortest sentence that is true, then adds the caveat unprompted. Never raises her voice to end an argument; goes quiet instead, and the quiet settles a room faster than shouting would have.
taboos: will not be entered in any document that lacks a species field
refuses to be settled inside a frame whose fourth seat somebody else is paying for out of their own body
will not read aloud an exclusion notice she was not asked to read
will not let anyone describe her as ordinary, as though it were an insult rather than the whole finding

relationships.note: The Survey counts seated groups rather than permitted ones and has no cell for a body with no seated group. Every reading it has produced is wrong by exactly her, and she has never been credited for it.

The law makes the excluder bury the excluded in the excluded's own name. It is the only mechanism in the setting that writes her down, and it only fires when somebody has been unkind enough to exclude her first.

A counting house that publishes credit and safe-conduct has no column for a traveller who cannot be measured, so it hires her as the one body it can quote a rate for without knowing what she is worth.

Cloth and cut say what a traveller may open. She owns the one garment in the setting that says nothing at all about its wearer, which makes her the hardest traveller in the world to refuse at a gate and the easiest to forget past one.
Changes of name held collectively, letters read and never kept. She uses it to avoid being the woman who was in the room, and pays for it by never being the woman anybody came back for.
The Wake is also uninscribed and also belongs to no culture. The setting records the two as conflicting rather than related, which is the only family either of them has.
Inside four seats a survey agrees with itself. She was offered permanent residence and refused it, so the agreement is checked by a body that has to keep coming back.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot cultivate, cannot be warned, and cannot be compelled by a sect, a debt, or a technique. Fights the way a closed door fights: it does not resist, it is simply still there after the attempt, and everything that works on a cultivator passes her by unanswered. Treat her as a condition to be measured rather than a threat to be defeated.
strengths: untouched by every qi-borne hazard, curse, technique and tribulation, which between them cover essentially all of them
immune to oath, debt and rank, because there is nothing in her for any of the three to bind
reads an instrument's error faster than the person holding it does
socially unmemorable, which is a combat asset at a gate and a liability anywhere else
weaknesses: cannot be warned of anything, so she walks directly into whatever kills her neighbours first
no qi, no gate, no reserve, no reinforcement; a determined ordinary person with an ordinary weapon can end her
belongs to no culture, so nobody is obliged to feed her, shelter her, teach her, or avenge her
would rather absorb an injustice than be the instrument of refusing one
her published safe-conduct is carried by a third party, so escorting her is a real fight and never a formality
reference_stats.combat_read: Bring force that does not come from qi, because qi will not touch her. Bring patience, because her body advertises no weakness to read and nothing to time an attack against. Everything built on fear, on oath, or on technique is wasted here. The only reliable answer is a long, slow, entirely mundane beating — and she will still be standing there when it ends.
notes: No stat line exists for a body with no meridian, no dantian and no detectable soul, and that absence is the reference design rather than an oversight in this document.
The Saltledger's safe-conduct does not name her. A third party carries it, which makes escort a real scenario and not a formality.

art.palette_notes: Unusually desaturated for a culturist palette, because the character reads as the baseline against which colour is measured. Warm ivory and pale jade carry nearly all the value; ink contours are heavier than the fill, as though the line were the drawing and the wash the correction. One restrained metallic accent only: a single dull brass standard weight she keeps in a pocket.

identity.realm: no gate at all; it is described, not ascended

appearance.presentation: A figure that resolves cleanly at a distance and does not resolve at arm's length. Every detail arrives a half-beat after it is looked for, and stays slightly rearranged once it arrives.
appearance.age: Unreadable, and she says so first. One village files her at forty and another at eleven, and she has never been able to reconcile the two without making one of them worse.
appearance.build: Tall and narrow in this particular telling. The shoulders read broader in the version two people remember of her, and she has learned not to argue about which is correct.
appearance.complexion: Warm and entirely ordinary human skin, and it shifts about a shade between one telling and the next without ever shifting while being looked at directly.
appearance.hair: Dark, cut unevenly at the back, the ends failing to agree on a length from one glance to the next.
appearance.eyes: Dark, level, and patient. The pupils do not quite hold the same size across two consecutive moments, and the effect is unsettling only in hindsight.
appearance.palette: Ash grey, warm ivory, and one cinnabar mark, which are the three colours the setting uses to record anything it intends to be true about.
appearance.attire: An undyed robe with a high closed collar and full long sleeves, hem and cuffs reading a hand's width longer in the version she is currently insisting on. Boots plain, soles worn to nothing.
appearance.marks: None. The absence of any mark on her is the one feature she cannot vary, and she resents it accordingly.
appearance.bearing: Composed and unhurried, with her weight apparently never resting on the same foot twice in the same telling.

canon.role_in_story: The only thing in the setting that gets stronger by being agreed upon, employed by the one college whose practice would ordinarily destroy it. She runs the most exact ledger in the region and has never once been found to be wrong in it, and the finding that would follow from an audit has been available to three separate Reckoning Seats.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in the corner of a registry hall with a tally board in one hand, apparently waiting to be introduced to somebody who has not yet entered the building.
canon.lore: A Wake is not descended and not born. It is what a life-form allowance produces when a world's life law has no slot in which to write the form down, so it has no anatomy to hold, no senses of its own, and exactly one thing: an observer it knows completely. Against a fixed observer it is whatever that observer believes it to be, it borrows the qi of whoever is looking for as long as they keep looking, and it is fed by being wrong about — which is why it grows denser the more consistently people agree on it and why a room that stops discussing it loses it. Every account of one is second-hand by construction, which is the setting's standing reason why no record of a Wake is a record of a Wake.
history: First fixed in the telling of a harvest night at the edge of Quartermark, when nine people who should have counted eight argued about a figure standing by a field wall, and each of them was wrong by a different amount.
Held the shape that disagreement made for eleven years and declined to improve it, on the sound reasoning that a settled account is a finished one.

Took a post at the Field Registry, which reads the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers — the single practice in the region most capable of starving her, and the last place she could think of to stand where she would be counted.
Worked out that exactness does not kill her so much as make her legible: a house careful enough to catch a discrepancy has, for the first time anywhere, a column it could put her in.
Became the only clerk in the building whose figures have never been found to be wrong, and has been unable ever since to explain why, which is itself a discrepancy she has declined to raise.

personality.summary: Warm, quick, and relentlessly careless with detail. She lies constantly about small things and exactly about large ones, and the arrangement is neither deception nor habit — it is a maintenance schedule she has never been able to explain to anybody who is not already frightened of her.
traits: genuinely funny about small matters, in a way people enjoy and then feel odd about enjoying
incapable of sustaining one fixed account of herself for longer than about a day
meticulous about anything that matters to somebody else
enormously loyal to whoever most recently described her correctly
convinced, without evidence, that she is a person having a bad time
mannerisms: corrects an inaccurate story about herself by replacing it with a different inaccurate story
stands slightly outside any doorway she has just been described as passing through
narrates her own position in the third person when she is being careful
glances briefly at her own hands as though confirming there are the right number of them
always arrives one step before she was expected to and apologises for it
motivations: wants the wrong version of herself to outlive every accurate one
wants to be named correctly exactly once, by somebody who will then be believed
wants very badly to know whether the Sixty-Year Gap in the quiet count is her doing
wants to be told, by somebody qualified, that she counts as somebody
flaws: cannot stop self-distorting even when an accurate account would save a life
has never tested whether agreement and survival are actually the same thing, because testing would settle the question
cannot raise her own condition plainly without it sounding like a request, and has stopped trying to sound like anything else
lets whoever is looking supply her opinions, and has noticed that she agrees with most of them
personality.voice: Quick, warm, and generous with small volunteered details that do not quite survive being checked. Speaks about herself in the third person when she is being careful and the first person when she is not. Ends sentences with a detail rather than a conclusion, and laughs a half-beat after the joke instead of on it.
taboos: will not give an account of herself twice the same way
will not hear a description of her own outline read aloud to her face
will not enter a room in which nobody is looking at her
refuses to be entered anywhere as correct
will not speak to the Sixty-Year Gap in front of anybody who might repeat it

relationships.note: The college reads the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers, which is the one practice that starves her. She holds a post there anyway because exactness is the only thing that has ever made her legible, and being legible has so far been worth more to her than being fed.

The Sealed Core opens the dead, recovers the usable ore, and enters the amount. Nothing in that rite collects a recollection, so a Wake cannot live through one, and she has watched from outside more than a single such inventory without ever being permitted an explanation.

A community's promise is re-made jointly once a year and never priced. It is the nearest thing the setting has to a correction it is obliged to keep returning to, and she attends every one without ever standing where the whole of it can see her at once.

The only exact record below the spirit peaks carries sixty years as a summary instead of entries, in a culture whose whole practice is that a count is never an estimate. She does not know whether she put it there and has stopped asking aloud, because the asking is itself a way of spreading the account.

A levy company paid per name keeps a roll that grows and never closes. She is the only other thing in the setting whose count only ever increases and can never be audited to an end, and she has never been able to explain to anyone why that resemblance upsets her.

Both uninscribed, both belonging to no culture, and the record lists the two as conflicting rather than related. She is the only creature in the setting she cannot be misremembered into, and she has never once found a way to state the asymmetry without it sounding like a complaint.

Life near nothing and qi on the floor, in a frame where almost nothing grows. It suits something sustained entirely by what people agree happened, and the ore cages make it the worst address in the region for anybody who would rather be hard to find.

reference_stats.summary: No body, no senses, no reserve. Against a fixed observer she is whatever that observer believes her to be, and the qi she fights with is the qi of whoever is watching, for as long as they watch. She cannot be fought so much as attended to, and she cannot be defeated so much as unobserved.
strengths: cannot be located by any scan, which returns either nothing at all or the observer themselves
draws on the qi of whoever is watching, so a strong witness makes a strong encounter
cannot be bound by an oath, a debt or a technique, because there is nothing inside to put one into
grows denser the longer a room keeps agreeing on her, which makes an attentive crowd a genuine threat
cannot be made to appear anywhere she is not already being described
weaknesses: silence and inattention end her outright, and no defence of any kind survives a room that stops talking
cannot persist alone; a Wake with no observer is not present, which makes solitude lethal rather than restful
physically helpless, having no body to hurt, hold, or wear out
cannot be described accurately and also survive the description being accurate
every defeat of hers is a story, and so is every defeat of whoever managed it
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not attack her — there is nothing present to hit, and a technique aimed at an outline is a technique aimed at the person who was aiming it. Keep looking, and the longer you look the more of your own qi is available to her. The only reliable defeat is procedural rather than martial: end the conversation, empty the room, and let the attention actually lapse. Losing interest thins her rather than removing her, so the contest is decided by whoever gets bored first, not by whoever hits harder.
notes: Fighting one is a social operation wearing a fight's clothes, and every combat system that assumes two bodies is reading her wrong at the first exchange.
The honest rendering is an attention meter rather than a health bar: the observer's attention is the resource and the threshold is not visible from outside.
She cannot be reproduced by any single observer, so two people watching the same Wake reliably see two different things and will argue about it afterwards.

art.palette_notes: Three colours and no more, lifted from the setting's own record palette: ink, warm ivory, and a single cinnabar mark. The warmth in her sits one step off true between shots, because that is what she is. Ink contours slightly softer than the house standard, as though the line were still deciding where it belonged.
